title: Graphs, symmetry, coordinates, and intercepts
section: Graphs in the xy-Plane ▷ Graphs and symmetry
terms: graph; vertical-line test; horizontal-line test; abscissa; ordinate; intercept; even function; odd function; reflection.

exposition.text:
The graph of f is {(x, f(x)) : x ∈ dom f}. A plane relation is a function of x exactly when
each vertical line meets it at most once; an injective function additionally passes the horizontal-
line test. An x-intercept has ordinate 0; a y-intercept has abscissa 0. Intercepts need not be
crossings: a graph can merely touch an axis.
Reflection across the y-axis replaces x by −x. On a domain symmetric about 0, an even func-
tion satisfies f(−x) = f(x) and an odd function satisfies f(−x) = −f(x). Reflection across
y = x interchanges a bijection’s graph with its inverse’s graph. Symmetry of a relation about
the x-axis generally conflicts with being a function unless all its ordinates are zero.

question.text:
A function f : R → R is even and satisfies f(x + 2) = −f(x) for every x. Which value must be
zero?
(A) f(0) (B) f (1) (C) f(2) (D) f(4) (E) f (1/2)

solution.text:
At x = −1, the relation gives f(1) = −f (−1). Evenness gives f(−1) = f (1), so f (1) = 0.
The function cos(πx/2) meets the hypotheses and makes the other listed values nonzero.

question.text:
2 2
For how many real values of a is the relation y + 2y = x + a the graph of a real-valued function
whose domain is all of R?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) Infinitely many

solution.text:
2 2
Completing the square gives (y + 1) = x + a + 1. For any fixed a, sufficiently large |x|
makes the right side positive, yielding two distinct values of y. Thus the vertical-line test
always fails.

question.text:
A function f is symmetric about both lines x = 1 and x = 4. Which positive number must be a
period of f?
(A) 6 (B) 1 (C) 3 (D) 2 (E) 4

solution.text:
The symmetries give f (2 − x) = f(x) and f(8 − x) = f(x). Composing the two reflections
yields f(x + 6) = f (x). For example cos(π(x − 1)/3) rules out the smaller listed periods.

question.text:
If f is odd and g(x) = f(x − 2) + 3, about which point is the graph of g centrally symmetric?
(A) (−2, −3) (B) (0, 0) (C) (2, −3) (D) (−2, 3) (E) (2, 3)

solution.text:
For any h, g(2 + h) + g(2 − h) = f (h) + f (−h) + 6 = 6. Thus opposite points have midpoint
(2, 3).

question.text:
2
How many intercept points does the graph y = (x − 1)/(x − 1) have with the two coordinate
axes combined?
(A) 1 (B) 4 (C) 3 (D) 0 (E) 2

solution.text:
The graph is y = x + 1 with the point at x = 1 removed. Its intercepts are (−1, 0) and (0, 1);
the canceled root x = 1 is not an intercept.

question.text:
−1
An odd function f : R → R is bijective. Which property must the graph of f have?
(A) Symmetry about the x-axis
(B) Symmetry about the y-axis
(C) Symmetry about the origin
(D) Symmetry about the line y = x
(E) A horizontal tangent at the origin

solution.text:
−1 −1
If f(x) = y, oddness gives f (−x) = −y. Inverting gives f (−y) = −f (y), so the in-
verse is odd. Its graph is the reflection of the original graph across y = x, but that does not
make the inverse graph itself symmetric about that line. No differentiability is assumed.
